regions.finding: The article introduces the CuBr-mediated homologation of optically active terminal propargylic alcohols with paraformaldehyde; background transformations and cited prior methods are contextual and are not counted as new target experiments.

Five distinct arrows were inventoried as cited starting-material-preparation literature examples: alkynol alkylation, alkyne reduction, asymmetric epoxidation, epoxy-alcohol chlorination, and n-BuLi conversion to a terminal propargylic alcohol. Generic R groups and absent quantities/yields remain unresolved.

Three distinct arrows were inventoried as cited starting-material-preparation literature examples: ethynylmagnesium-bromide addition to nonanal, chromium(VI) oxidation to the ynone, and BINOL/LiAlH4 reduction. Missing quantities, times, yields, and some stereochemical assignments remain unresolved.

regions.region: lower-right prose and general experimental statement
regions.finding: The prose identifies Scheme 3 as work in this study and states the general argon/solvent handling context. Scheme 3 is linked across page 2, and the argon statement supplies evidence to the nine homologation records without creating a separate experiment.

unresolved: Scheme 1 contains generic R groups, and the source does not report arrow-specific quantities or yields.
Scheme 2 omits quantities, most times, workups, and yields; the final arrow does not state an absolute configuration or ee on this page.
The article discusses cited starting-material methods, but no Supporting Information was explicitly supplied or associated.

regions.finding: Four independent stages were extracted: (S,S)-complex reduction (100%), desilylation to the corresponding propargylic alcohol (99%, 98% ee), (R,R)-complex reduction (97%), and the opposite desilylation (99%, 98% ee). Each arrow is a separate partial reported experiment.

regions.region: right column, typical (R)-2a procedure and following (S)-2a/(R)-2b prose
regions.finding: The typical 120 °C, 2 h homologation, evaporation, and silica-gel purification were linked to the corresponding table records. The (S)-2a and beginning of (R)-2b procedures were merged with their table rows rather than duplicated.

All four (S)-series rows were extracted independently with starting-material ee, product yield, product ee, and specific rotation. Their detailed prose procedures on pages 2-3 were associated with the same row records.

All five (R)-series rows were extracted independently. Entries 3 and 5 retain distinct records although both produce (R)-2c, because the starting ee, isolated mass, yield, product ee, and optical rotation differ.

unresolved: Scheme 3 reports catalyst loading, solvent system, yields, and final ee but omits substrate/reagent quantities, temperature, time, workup, and yield basis.
Candidate SMILES for chiral substrates/products omit absolute stereochemical encoding and remain structure-unverified.
The detailed (R)-2b procedure continues on page 3.

regions.region: left column, continuation of (R)-2b and procedures for (S)-2b, both (R)-2c runs, and (S)-2c
regions.finding: The continuation and four procedure blocks were merged into their existing Table 1/2 rows. The two (R)-2c experiments remain separate because one starts at 94% ee and the repeated experiment starts at 98% ee.

The two phenyl-substrate homologations were merged with Table 1/2. For (S)-2d, the prose visually prints '225 mg (77 mg, 96% ee)' while Table 1 reports 77% yield; the table yield is structured and the discrepancy is retained as unresolved.

No additional experiments are reported in the acknowledgements or reference list. The cited works are bibliographic context and were not converted into experiments beyond the explicitly drawn Scheme 1/2 arrows.

unresolved: The (S)-2d prose/table expression contains an apparent 77 mg versus 77% typographical discrepancy.
The (R)-2b heading visually contains an apparent duplicated locant; the source wording was preserved in a note rather than silently repaired.
No Supporting Information was explicitly supplied or associated, so missing procedural details cannot be filled.
